summary: Saint Lucia is visa-free for citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada and China, among others. EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU waiver agreement; the UK and Canadian governments say their citizens get up to six weeks, which the Immigration Department can extend, and Saint Lucia publishes no figure for other passports; CARICOM nationals other than Haitians need no visa. Citizens of other listed countries and territories, including India, need a visa that the Department of External Affairs' list (dated July 2024) gives as issued at the port of entry, and those it marks as required prior to arrival need a visa arranged through a Saint Lucian mission before traveling.

tips.text: EU citizens may stay 90 days in any 180 under the EU agreement, but the UK and Canadian governments say their citizens are admitted for up to six weeks. The UK Foreign Office says that to stay longer you must go to the Immigration Department in Castries.
The UK government says it is illegal for anyone in Saint Lucia, including children, to dress in camouflage clothing.
Traffic drives on the left, according to Canada's travel advice, and the UK government says visitors without a Saint Lucian driving licence must get a temporary driving permit.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and China, among others, enter visa-free, and so do CARICOM nationals other than Haitians. Citizens of other listed countries and territories, including India, Kenya, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, need a visa that the Department of External Affairs' list (dated July 2024) gives as issued at the port of entry. Nationalities the list marks as required prior to arrival must obtain a visa from a Saint Lucian mission before traveling.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Saint Lucia without a visa?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. EU citizens may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period under the EU–Saint Lucia waiver agreement, and Saint Lucia’s visa list gives Norwegians and Swiss the same. The UK and Canadian governments say their citizens are admitted for up to six weeks. For other visa-free passports Saint Lucia publishes no figure. The UK Foreign Office says that to stay longer you must go to the Immigration Department in Castries.

faq.question: Is there an arrival form for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Yes — the online Embarkation/Disembarkation (ED) form, which replaced the paper immigration and customs card in 2022. Complete it no more than 72 hours before you travel, one per family or group, and show the emailed receipt with your passport at immigration.

faq.question: Is camouflage clothing really banned in Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says it is illegal for anyone, including children, to dress in camouflage clothing in Saint Lucia.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Only if you are coming from a country listed as a yellow fever transmission risk, according to the UK Foreign Office; WHO's country list sets the requirement for travellers aged 9 months or over arriving from such countries.

faq.question: Does CARICOM free movement apply in Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Saint Lucia's visa list says nationals of the other CARICOM member states, except Haiti, need no visa. No official source we could read states the length of stay they are granted.
